data.narrative:
Tenna Systems, a seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by Avner and Gabriel Bendheim, has raised $13.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 10 comparable companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Shield AI, filtered for sector and stage alignment.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The Stage-Progression approach uses total raised ($13.5M, proxied as $14M) as a base and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $34M. The Peer-Median method examines 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Stark Defence at $4.0B, UFORCE at $1.0B, Singularity at $400M, NODA AI at $125M), producing a median valuation of $700M and a range of $125M to $4.0B. These methods generate a wide dispersion reflecting stage and maturity variance within the peer set.

The triangulated analysis yields a median of $367M with a low-end estimate of $29M and high-end of $805M. This spread reflects material uncertainty around the company's technology differentiation and market opportunity relative to better-capitalized competitors. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively near raised capital, while peer-median valuation is driven substantially by UFORCE's $1.0B seed valuation, a significant outlier. Key unknowns include Tenna's product-market fit trajectory, customer traction, and competitive positioning within a crowded defense-tech landscape.
